objective: Prove that on a closed orientable surface every odd cluster of a twisted sector shields the twists dual to the boundary classes of its neighbourhood, which span the radical of its period lattice under the intersection form, so that the counts of an event are equal for twists differing by the span of these duals over its odd clusters; prove that surface automorphisms map events and twists to events and twists with equal counts; and record that planar duality gives no relation inside a genus-2 square tiling.
status: Proved by TWIST-MAP-20261023-001A-P001 (V1 prose proof; exhaustive L(2,1,2,1) and sampled checks; four controls rejected). On every closed orientable surface the count of orientations with a given skeleton (set of cyclic edges) factorizes in each twist as c times A: c counts orientations of the skeleton in which every skeleton edge is cyclic, A counts acyclic orientations of the cover of the graph with every cluster shrunk to a point (an odd cluster has one node, so twists at it do not enter). Parallel edges of the shrunken graph and series edges of a cluster can be merged. Twists whose series-reduced clusters and parallel-reduced shrunken graphs are isomorphic up to switching give equal counts, skeleton by skeleton. The boundary circles of a cluster span the radical of its lattice, so the wall group of a label (the duals of the radicals of its odd clusters) preserves its count; automorphisms act; on the L-shaped genus-2 tilings planar duality relates no two counts of one surface.
title: Proof: the wall group and the symmetries
